site.notes:
This general site was originally cored by Whitehead (1972), and no radiocarbon dates were obtained at that time. This site is located east of the Dismal Swamp Canal, for which construction began in 1793 CE, and substantial
disturbance of forests has occurred since that time (including logging and hydrologic changes associated with the canal). Our reanalysis of Whitehead samples suggested that his core included samples of middle Holocene to deglacial age. To generate a higher resolution record, we revisited the site in 2020 and collected both a Russian peat core  (GDS-77R-11-19-20) and a freeze core (GDS-77F-11-19-2020).

dataset.datasetname: Paleoecological data from Great Dismal Swamp GDS-77
dataset.datasetnotes: Final dataset is a composite of two cores (77R and 77F). USGS IPDS# IP-164096

collectionunit.notes: The samples from 1-35 cm were collected from a freeze core, whereas samples from 36.5-205.5 cm were taken from a Russian core at the same site. Because the site has been drained substantially by the nearby Dismal Swamp Canal (since the late 18th century), the upper part of the section has a "coffee-grounds" texture that is not well captured by the Russian corer. We present the pollen data as a composite of the two cores, with tie points established by a combination of LOI, radiocarbon dates, and comparison of pollen assemblages with other, less-disturbed cores from Great Dismal Swamp.
